blocks.task_summary: Find angle JDL in triangle JDL given bearing 034 degrees from J to D, JL = 500 km east, and angle JLD = 25 degrees.

evidence.basis: Let N be North. NJD = 34 degrees OR DJL = 56 degrees (must be labelled or indicated in diagram): (A1). JDL = 99 degrees A1. Note: Accept 11pi/20, 1.73 (radians).

blocks.task_summary: Find the standard deviation s of a normal distribution with mean 32 given that the interquartile range is 0.28 mm.
method_path: Recognize area below Q1 or above Q3 is 0.25, so P(D < Q1) = 0.25
Obtain inverse normal z-value: z = inv_Phi(0.75) = 0.674489...
Express IQR = Q3 - Q1 = (mu + z*sigma) - (mu - z*sigma) = 2*z*sigma = 0.28
Round to 3 significant figures: sigma = 0.208 mm
accepted_alternatives: Method 1: Compute Q1 = 31.86 and Q3 = 32.14 from IQR = 0.28 and symmetry about mean 32; set up standardised equation (Q3 - 32)/sigma = 0.674489... or (31.86 - 32)/sigma = -0.674489...; solve for sigma = 0.208 mm. Alternative: equate normal CDF to 0.25 or 0.75 directly using GDC.
Method 2: Express Q1 = 32 - 0.674489...*sigma and Q3 = 32 + 0.674489...*sigma; use IQR = Q3 - Q1 = 2 * 0.674489...*sigma = 0.28; solve for sigma = 0.208 mm.

evidence.basis: Q1 = 31.86 OR Q3 = 32.14 (A1); recognition that area under the normal curve below Q1 or above Q3 is 0.25 OR area between Q1 and Q3 is 0.5 (M1); z = -0.674489... OR z = 0.674489... (A1); (31.86-32)/sigma = -0.674489... OR (32.14-32)/sigma = 0.674489... (A1); sigma = 0.207564... approx 0.208 (mm) A1.

blocks.task_summary: Find positive constants a and b given that the coefficient of x^6 in (ax^3+b)^8 is 448 and in (ax^3+b)^10 is 2880.
method_path: Write the general term of (ax^3+b)^8: C(8,r)(ax^3)^(8-r) b^r = C(8,r) a^(8-r) b^r x^(24-3r)
Set exponent of x to 6: 24-3r=6 implies r=6, or symmetrically r=2
Write the x^6 coefficient equation for n=8: C(8,2) a^6 b^2 = 448
Simplify: 28 a^6 b^2 = 448 implies a^6 b^2 = 16
Write general term of (ax^3+b)^10, set 30-3r=6 implies r=8 (or r=2)
Write the x^6 coefficient equation for n=10: C(10,2) a^8 b^2 = 2880
Simplify: 45 a^8 b^2 = 2880 implies a^8 b^2 = 64
Solve the system, e.g. divide: a^2 = 4 implies a = 1/2 (a>0)
Substitute back to find b: b^2 = 4 implies b = 2 (b>0)
accepted_alternatives: Using r=6 instead of r=2 for n=8 expansion (or r=8 instead of r=2 for n=10), by symmetry of binomial coefficients.
Solving the system graphically instead of algebraically.

evidence.basis: product of a binomial coefficient, a power of ax^3 and a power of b seen (M1)
evidence of correct term chosen: for n=8: r=2 (or r=6) OR for n=10: r=2 (or r=8) (A1)
correct equations (may include powers of x) A1A1
attempt to solve their system in a and b algebraically or graphically (M1)

blocks.task_summary: Find the smallest positive integer n such that z^n = −i for z = cos(11π/18) + i sin(11π/18).
method_path: Apply De Moivre's theorem: z^n = cos(11πn/18) + i sin(11πn/18)
Set z^n = −i and equate arguments: 11πn/18 = 3π/2 + 2kπ, k ∈ ℤ
Find least positive integer solution: k = 2 ⇒ n = 9
accepted_alternatives: Equate imaginary parts instead of arguments: sin(11πn/18) = −1 along with cos(11πn/18) = 0

evidence.basis: attempt to use De Moivre's theorem (M1); attempt to consider imaginary part (M1) OR attempt to consider argument of −i (M1); 11πn/18 = 3π/2 + 2kπ or 110n = 270 + 360k (A1); n = 9 A1

blocks.task_summary: Describe a single geometric transformation applied to z on the Argand diagram that results in z^10.
method_path: Find angular difference: arg(z^10) − arg(z) = π/9 − 11π/18 = −π/2
State transformation: rotation about the origin by −π/2 (clockwise π/2, or 3π/2 counterclockwise)
accepted_alternatives: Recognise z^10 = z^9 × z and use z^9 = −i from part (a); multiplication by −i corresponds to rotation by 3π/2 (or −π/2) about the origin.

evidence.basis: EITHER arg(z^10) = 55π/9 = π/9 (A1); recognising that the difference between arg(z^10) and arg(z) is needed (M1); arg(z^10)−arg(z) = −π/2 OR recognising that z^10 = z^9 × z (M1); z^9 = e^{i·3π/2} (A1); THEN a rotation 3π/2 OR π/2 clockwise about the origin A1

blocks.task_summary: Given that 18 out of 150 positive test results are false positives, estimate the population proportion p with the gene.
method_path: Recognize the conditional probability P(G' | positive) = 18/150
Express via law of total probability: 0.02(1−p) / (0.95p + 0.02(1−p)) = 18/150
accepted_alternatives: METHOD 2: Set up system 0.95pS = 132 and (1−p)(0.02)S = 18, solve for p.
METHOD 3: Compute number with gene = 132/0.95 ≈ 138.95, number without = 18/0.02 = 900, total ≈ 1038.95, then p ≈ 138.95/1038.95 ≈ 0.134.

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: (M1) recognizing conditional probability; (A1)(A1) correct numerator and denominator in 0.02(1−p)/(0.95p+0.02(1−p)) = 18/150; A1 p = 0.134. METHOD 2: (M1) system of equations; (A1) 0.95pS = 132 and (1−p)(0.02)S = 18; (M1) solve; A1 p = 0.134. METHOD 3: (M1) find numbers; (A1) 132/0.95 and 18/0.02; (M1) find proportion; A1 p = 0.134.

recognizing angle between normal and direction vector is π/2−α (seen anywhere) (M1)
attempt to substitute into the formula for the angle between two vectors to form an equation in α (M1); 12+2cosα−sinα=√17√14 sinα
α=0.932389… → α=0.932 A1; Note: maximum (A1)(A1)(A1)(A1)(M1)(M1)A0 for correct answer in degrees (54.4219…°)

blocks.task_summary: Prove by contradiction that p² − 8q − 11 ≠ 0 for any integers p, q.
method_path: Assume p² − 8q − 11 = 0 for p, q ∈ ℤ.
Show p must be odd by parity argument.
Simplify to 2k² + 2k = 4q + 5, with LHS even and RHS odd.
State contradiction: even ≠ odd, therefore original statement holds.
accepted_alternatives: For the parity step: Either argue p² = 2(4q+5)+1 ⇒ p² odd ⇒ p odd, OR argue p even ⇒ p² − 8q even, contradicting 11 odd, so p must be odd. Also accept work based on p = 2k − 1 instead of 2k + 1.

evidence.basis: M1: 'Assume p² − 8q − 11 = 0, (p,q ∈ ℤ)'. R1 (parity): 'p² = 8q + 11 = 2(4q+5) + 1 so p² odd ⇒ p odd' or 'p even ⇒ p² − 8q = even which is a contradiction so p is odd'. M1: 'p = 2k + 1, k ∈ ℤ'. (A1): '(2k+1)² = 8q + 11 → 4k² + 4k + 1 = 8q + 11'. A1: '2k² + 2k = 4q + 5 or equivalent with one side odd and one side even'. R1: 'a contradiction as LHS is even and RHS is odd'.

blocks.task_summary: Find the cross-sectional area of the gutter by first determining the width w (via cosine rule, sine rule, or right-triangle trigonometry with θ/2), then computing the area as (sector OAB − triangle OAB + rectangle CDBA) or as (2 × trapezium CGOA + sector OAB), giving approximately 294 cm².
accepted_alternatives: Use sine rule 12/sin(θ) = w/sin(π−θ)/2 to find w
Use right-triangle trig with angle θ/2 and hypotenuse 12 to find w/2
Area via 2 × trapezium CGOA + sector OAB
Area via rectangle CDFE + 2 × triangle EOA + sector OAB

evidence.basis: First three marks for finding w: evidence of using cosine rule OR sine rule (M1); w² = 12²+12²−2·12·12·cos(2.08) OR 12/sin(2.08) = w/sin(0.530796...) (A1); w ≈ 20.6977 or w/2 ≈ 10.3488 (A1). OR using trig ratios in right triangle with angle 2.08/2 and side w/2 (M1); sin(2.08/2) = (w/2)/12 (A1); w ≈ 20.6977 (A1).

(segment AHB =) sector OAB − triangle OAB (M1); = ½·12²·2.08 − ½·12²·sin(2.08) = 149.76 − 62.8655... = 86.8944... (A1); valid approach to find total cross-sectional area (M1); sector OAB − triangle OAB + rectangle CDBA = 86.8944... + 10w = 86.8944... + 206.977... (A1 for final area 294 cm²).

OR trapezium CGOA approach: trapezium CGOA (M1); = ½(20.6977... + 10 + 10 − 12cos(1.04)) × 10 ≈ 72.0557 (A1); valid approach to total area (M1); 2 × trapezium CGOA + sector OAB = 2(72.0557...) + ½·12²·2.08 = 144.111... + 149.76 (A1 for final 294 cm²).

blocks.task_summary: Determine whether the gutter overflows by computing gutter volume (600 × cross-sectional area ≈ 176,323–176,658 cm³) and comparing with the total rainfall over 60 seconds, given R′(t) = 50 cos(2πt/5) + 3000. The rainfall ∫₀⁶⁰ R′(t) dt = 180,000 cm³ exceeds the gutter volume, so it overflows.
accepted_alternatives: Use minimum of R′(t) = 2950 cm³/s to bound rainfall from below: 60 × 2950 = 177,000 > gutter volume
Solve ∫₀ᵀ R′(t) dt = gutter volume to find T ≈ 58.8 s < 60 s

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: volume of gutter = 176323 OR 176658 (OR 600×their area) (A1); recognising rainfall can be represented by an integral (M1); ∫₀⁶⁰ R′(t) dt (A1); rainfall over 60 seconds = 180000 (cm³) (A1); the gutter will overflow because the rainfall > gutter volume (A1).

METHOD 2 (alternative): volume of gutter (A1); recognition that cosine has a minimum value of −1 (M1); R′(t) ≥ −1×50 + 3000 = 2950 cm³/s (A1); rainfall over 60 seconds ≥ 177000 (A1); overflow because rainfall > gutter volume (A1).

METHOD 3 (alternative): volume of gutter (A1); recognising rainfall as integral (M1); attempt to solve 60 > 58.8 OR ∫₀ᵀ R′(t) dt = 176658 (M1); time to reach overflow = 58.7875... or 58.8990... (A1); gutter overflows because 60 > 58.8 or 60 > 58.9 (A1).
